Physical Defence Down (or Phys Def Down) is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles and Future Connected. It increases the amount of physical taken by the victim by a percentage. The math of the debuff differs depending on whether it is applied to a party member or an enemy. For an example where the debuff's percentage is 25%: * On a party member with 200 physical defence, the value will be multiplied to equal 150. * On an enemy with 30% physical defence, the value will be subtracted to equal -5%. Physical Def Down can be inflicted with an when equipping Phys Def Down s.

Physical Defence Up is a buff in Xenoblade Chronicles. It raises the user's physical defence, thus reducing damage taken from physical attacks. Whether Physical Defence Up is better than is a complex matter that depends on many factors. Generally, because Physical Defense Up is a percentage-based boost to the user's defence, it will be ineffective if the user's defence is low to start with. This buff does not have an explanation associated with it, perhaps because there is no art that applies it by itself.

Proto Dora is a boss in Xenosaga Episode I - Der Wille zur Macht. This boss is accompanied by two Schutz mechs. On its first turn, it activates a Beam Shield which initially reduces all beam damage to 0 for the rest of the fight. However, it is possible to damage and eventually break the shield by hitting it with enough beam attacks. After that attack it will use a piercing Steel Press that hits all party members that are not in A.G.W.S. mechs. It can attack one target using either the pierce (P) attack Steel Crusher or the ether (E) attack Beam. Rare Blades are a type of in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. Like Legendary Blades, they are fully-realized characters with their own designs, skills, and personalities; like Common Blades, they are not part of the main plot and can only be obtained by resonating with Core Crystals. Uniquely, they also have special quests ("Blade Quests") dedicated to their character arc, which often play a part in unlocking their . Some Rare Blades are guaranteed to be found in specific Core Crystals earned by various means, but most are simply within the same random pool that Common Blades are drawn from. Quiet Moments are events in Future Connected similar to s in the main game. Watching them is completely optional and, unlike Heart-to-Hearts, give no rewards such as . Games in the Xeno series use randomness as a factor in many aspects. Examples common throughout the series include the amount of an attack deals, the actions taken by -controlled characters and enemies, item rewards from , and the animations of objects in the overworld. As is typically the case for such games, randomness is handled using a (pseudo-)random number generator, or RNG for short. These use mathematical algorithms which take in a number and produce a different number, statistically uncorrelated with the number which was taken in.
